title: Turn a saved recipe reel into a grocery order
summary: Forward Muse the Instagram reel you saved for Sunday dinner and get a grouped grocery list, minus what you already have, ready to order for delivery.
problem: You save a recipe reel on Instagram for Sunday dinner. Normally that reel dies in your Saved folder. With Muse it becomes groceries at your door.
prerequisites: Make purchases, confirm with you first
steps: Save or forward the reel to Muse, in the Muse app or by messaging it in WhatsApp.
Muse watches the reel, transcribes it and extracts the full ingredient list with quantities.
It checks the list against the pantry staples it remembers from earlier conversations (olive oil, cumin, rice) so you do not rebuy them.
It builds a clean grocery list grouped by store section: produce, dairy, spices.
If you have named a store or connected a grocery service, it opens its cloud browser, fills the cart and pauses for your approval before checkout.
Checkout goes through Link by Stripe with a one-time virtual card, so your real card number never reaches the merchant.
result: Early testers found general web shopping is Muse's weakest area; one hands-on test could not complete a Costco run. This is most reliable when the store has a clean website and the items are common. Start with list generation before handing it your grocery money. Approval gates: One: the final cart review before it pays.
prompt: Here's a recipe reel I saved. Turn it into a grocery list for 4 servings, skip anything I already have, and order it from [store] for delivery tomorrow morning.

title: Plan a dinner party with a menu, timeline and invites
summary: Give Muse the date, headcount and vibe. It plans a scaled menu, remembers who cannot eat what.
problem: You are hosting six people on Saturday. Muse plans the menu, remembers who cannot eat what, and handles the invitations.
steps: Tell Muse the date, headcount and vibe, such as casual and Italian-ish.
Muse suggests a starter, main and dessert scaled to six, plus a shopping list and a prep timeline working backward from 7pm on Saturday.

It recalls dietary restrictions from past conversations. If you once mentioned that Priya is vegetarian and Dan is gluten-free, it flags the dishes that need adapting without you re-entering anything.
It drafts the invitation messages; you approve each one and it sends them through your connected messaging or email.
It can turn the whole plan into a printable checklist you keep on your phone in the kitchen.
result: Memory cuts both ways. Tell Muse to forget something and verify that it did. The upside is that the second dinner party is far easier than the first. Approval gates: Menu approval, then per-invite approval before anything sends.
prompt: I'm hosting a dinner party Saturday for 6. Plan an Italian-ish menu, build the shopping list and a prep timeline, and draft the invites. Remember everyone's dietary stuff.

title: Negotiate your internet bill down
summary: Give Muse your provider, what you pay and your ceiling. It researches competitor offers, negotiates with retention support in its browser.
problem: Your internet bill crept up to 89 dollars a month. You would never call to haggle. Muse does it while you are at lunch.
prerequisites: Access account settings, confirm changes first
steps: Tell Muse the provider, what you pay and what you would switch for.
Muse researches competitor pricing and current retention offers in the background.
It opens the provider's site or chat support in its browser and negotiates: citing competitor rates, asking for retention deals, escalating politely.
It reports back with the offer. Nothing is agreed without you.
The same playbook works for phone bills, insurance renewals and subscription cancellations.
result: Some providers require phone calls or identity steps Muse cannot pass, and success varies wildly by company. Treat this as experimental: wins are real but not guaranteed. Approval gates: Final offer approval. Tell it explicitly never to accept on your behalf.
prompt: My [provider] bill is $89/month. Negotiate it down. I'd accept anything under $65 for at least a year. Don't agree to anything without asking me first.

title: Handle buyer messages when selling your car
summary: Give Muse the listing, your asking price and your floor. It drafts a reply to every inquiry, counters lowballs with local comps and schedules viewings.
problem: You are selling your car on Marketplace. Buyers lowball. Muse negotiates every inquiry toward your target price without you touching your phone.
steps: Give Muse the listing: car details, asking price and your walk-away floor.
As buyer messages arrive, Muse drafts a reply to each: countering lowballs with comparable listings in your area, answering spec questions, proposing viewing times.
Every outbound message waits for your one-tap approval. You see the buyer, the offer and the proposed counter before anything sends.
When a buyer reaches your target, Muse flags it and asks whether to accept and schedule the handoff.
result: This was Meta's own launch demo, and in hands-on testing each Marketplace message still needed human review, which testers called friction. It is slower than a bot farm on purpose: no message goes out that you did not see. Approval gates: Every single outbound message.
prompt: I'm selling my 2019 Civic for $16,500. Handle buyer messages. Never accept below $14,500, counter lowballs with local comps, and get my approval on every reply.

title: Watch a price and buy at the right moment
summary: Name a product and a target price. Muse compares retailers, watches the price, pings you when it drops.
problem: You want a specific espresso machine. Muse watches prices across stores, buys at the right moment, and you are covered if the price drops further.
prerequisites: Make purchases, confirm with you first
steps: Name the product and your target price.
Muse compares options across retailers in its browser, specs, reviews and shipping times, and presents a shortlist.
It monitors the price. When it hits your target or a sale starts, it pings you.
You approve; Muse checks out with a one-time Link by Stripe virtual card.
Meta says Muse is the first agent covered by Link's purchase protections on eligible purchases: damaged or lost items, price-drop protection and no-fee returns.
result: This has the widest gap between demo and reality: a reviewer's real shopping task failed outright. Use it for simple single-retailer purchases first and keep the experimental label until reliability improves. Approval gates: Purchase approval, always.
prompt: I want the [model] espresso machine. Watch prices, alert me under $250, and buy it when I say go.

title: Draft replies to every Marketplace buyer
summary: Ten buyers ask the same five questions. Muse reads your listing details and drafts each reply; you approve from a queue.
problem: You flip furniture on Facebook Marketplace. Ten buyers message at once with the same five questions. Muse drafts every reply; you just approve.
steps: Connect Facebook and Messenger. Muse reads incoming buyer messages on your listings.
For each message it drafts a reply from the listing details it already knows: dimensions, price, pickup location and the times that work.
You get a queue of drafts. Tap approve on each; nothing sends without you.
The buy-side mirror is the deal watcher workflow, which watches for listings you want.
result: Bulk messaging is deliberately slow. Approval per message is a safety feature. This is leverage, not automation. Approval gates: Per message, by design.
prompt: Draft replies to all my Marketplace messages using my listing details. I'll approve each one before it sends.

title: Export your Instagram followers and map the clusters
summary: Ask Muse for a spreadsheet of your followers with bios and engagement signals, then a map of who follows whom.
problem: You are a creator or a small brand and you want to actually know your followers: not a count, but who is there, who follows whom, and where the clusters are.
steps: Ask Muse to export your Instagram followers into a spreadsheet: handles, bios, follower counts and engagement signals.
It goes further, examines followers of followers, maps the relationship graph and renders a visualisation of your audience clusters.
You get a file you own rather than a dashboard trapped in an app, plus the visual.
result: In the best-documented hands-on test the export stopped at 749 accounts and the tester could not tell whether that was an API limit or a cutoff, and the visualisation was attractive but not very functional. Keep exports small and verify row counts against the source. Approval gates: None needed; this is read-only work.
prompt: Export my Instagram followers to a spreadsheet with bios and engagement stats, then map the follower-of-follower relationships and visualize the clusters.

title: Triage your inbox every morning
summary: Muse reads new mail, drafts replies in your voice, flags what needs a decision and archives the noise. Start read-only, then drafts, then approved sends.
problem: You wake up to 80 emails. Muse has already read them, drafted replies to 30, flagged 5 that need you, and archived the noise.
steps: Connect email with granular permissions. Start read-only.
Each morning, or on demand from WhatsApp, Muse scans new mail, categorises it and drafts replies in your voice, learned from your sent folder.
You review a digest: drafts to approve, items needing decisions, FYIs. One tap per draft.
Over weeks it learns which senders matter and which threads you ignore, and starts pre-sorting before you ask.
result: This is the highest blast-radius workflow here: a misfired email is reputational damage, not a bad answer. Climb the ladder: read-only first, drafts second, approved sends third. Approval gates: Per-email send approval. Run read-only for a week before granting send.
prompt: Every weekday at 8am, triage my inbox. Draft replies, flag anything needing a decision, archive newsletters. Never send without my approval.

title: Fill out forms and registrations for you
summary: Forward Muse a form link or a photo of a paper form. It completes every field from the details it remembers and stops before signatures.
problem: School permission slips, camp registrations, insurance forms, job applications: the paperwork of life. Muse opens the sites and fills them out.
steps: Forward Muse the form link or a photo of a paper form, plus any details it does not have. It remembers your kids' names, birthdates, allergies and your address from earlier conversations.
Muse opens the form in its cloud browser and completes every field.
It stops at signatures, payments and anything legally binding; those come to you.
For recurring forms it can pre-fill and queue them on schedule.
result: Sites with aggressive anti-bot protection, CAPTCHAs or identity verification will block it. It works best on straightforward web forms. Approval gates: Pre-submission review, always. Signatures and payments are human-only.
prompt: Fill out this camp registration for [kid]. Use the details you have on file. Stop before anything that needs a signature or payment and show me the completed form.

title: Book and manage a recurring lesson or class
summary: Describe a recurring need once. Muse finds providers, books the first session with your approval, then manages rebooking.
problem: Book me tennis lessons every Tuesday at 6pm, said once, handled forever.
steps: Describe the recurring need in plain language: lessons, classes, reservations, tickets.
Muse finds providers, compares schedules and prices, and books the first one with your approval.
It then manages the series: rebooking, handling cancellations, finding substitutes when you are travelling (it has your calendar) and confirming each week.
Movie tickets, restaurant reservations and gym classes follow the same pattern.
result: Cancellation policies vary. Make sure Muse knows which bookings are refundable before it commits you to a series. Approval gates: First booking approval; the ongoing series runs on the rules you set.
prompt: Book me beginner tennis lessons every Tuesday at 6pm near [area], under $40/session. Handle rebooking and cancellations, and skip weeks I'm traveling.

title: A fitness plan that rebuilds itself when you fall behind
summary: Give Muse the goal. It builds a phased plan as a living document, tracks connected health data.
problem: Not a workout PDF you abandon by February. A plan that notices you stopped and adjusts.
steps: Tell Muse the goal: run a half marathon in October, or lose 15 pounds sustainably.
Muse builds a phased plan as a living document: training blocks, rest weeks, nutrition guidelines.
Connect health data and it tracks workouts, trends and plateaus.
When you travel, get sick or work explodes, it notices the gap and rewrites the plan, for example a rebuilt 8-week ramp instead of the original 12.
Weekly check-ins arrive in WhatsApp like a text from a coach.
result: It is a planner and an accountability layer, not a doctor. Good for structure and adaptation, not for medical advice or injury rehab. Approval gates: None structural, but keep health data sharing deliberate and minimal.
prompt: Build me a half-marathon plan for October. I'm currently running 10 miles a week. Check in weekly and rebuild the plan whenever I fall behind.

title: Turn a business idea into a 90-day plan
summary: Describe the idea in a sentence. Muse breaks it into workstreams with owners and deadlines, does the supplier and competitor research in the background.
problem: I want to start a candle business becomes a 90-day plan with tasks, deadlines and research, coordinated while you keep your day job.
steps: Describe the business idea in a sentence or two.
Muse breaks it into workstreams: market research, supplier sourcing, pricing, branding, legal basics and a launch checklist, each with an owner (you or Muse) and a deadline.
It does the legwork in the background: comparing suppliers, drafting product descriptions, researching competitors, building a simple budget spreadsheet.
Weekly it reports what is done, what is blocked on you and what is next, and adjusts the timeline when you fall behind.
Side chats keep workstreams separate while the main chat holds the full picture.
result: Muse can research and draft, but it cannot taste your candles or sign a lease. It is a chief of staff for the idea phase; execution still needs a human. Approval gates: Spending and legal or filing decisions come to you; research runs free.
prompt: I want to launch a soy candle business in 90 days. Build the full plan, do the supplier and competitor research, and check in every Monday with what's done and what needs me.

title: Watch Marketplace for the deal you want
summary: Describe the item, max price, radius and condition. Muse watches Marketplace, filters out the junk and messages you the moment a real match appears.
problem: You have been hunting a used Herman Miller chair under 400 dollars for months. Muse watches and pings you the minute one appears.
steps: Describe exactly what you want: item, maximum price, radius, condition.
Muse monitors Facebook Marketplace and other listing sites on a schedule.
The Ideas tab may suggest this itself. In testing, Muse noticed someone browsing office furniture and proposed recurring desk searches.
When a match appears you get a WhatsApp ping with the listing, price history where available, and a draft message to the seller.
You approve the message or the purchase. Muse never buys unprompted.
result: Set the frequency and price rules explicitly, or enthusiastic monitoring becomes notification spam. Approval gates: Outreach and purchase approvals.
prompt: Watch Marketplace for a used Herman Miller Aeron under $400 within 20 miles. Ping me immediately when one shows up.

title: Build a budget tracker or study guide you can keep
summary: Describe the deliverable and Muse builds it in its cloud workspace as a real file: an interactive tracker, a PDF study guide, a one-page site.
problem: You need a thing, not an answer: a budget tracker, a study guide for your certification exam, a one-page site for your garage sale.
steps: Describe the deliverable, for example a household spending tracker or a PMP study guide at two hours a day for six weeks.
Muse builds it in its cloud workspace with real files and real code: interactive spreadsheets, PDFs, HTML pages, small web apps.
It iterates with you conversationally, such as making the budget categories match your bank's.
The files live in your Muse workspace, downloadable and yours. If a service has a public API, Muse can wire the artifact to live data with credentials you provide.
result: First-version quality varies. Treat Muse like a talented junior who needs one round of feedback, not a senior shipping final work. Approval gates: None; this is pure creation. Review the output the way you would review a freelancer's.
prompt: Build me an interactive household budget tracker as a web page I can open on my phone. Categories: housing, food, transport, fun, savings.
